With YNAB I paid basically $100 a year BUT the goal is to save money, right, so you have to cut spending anywhere you can, UX/UI is a luxury so I ditched YNAB after 10 years with them. I’ve played around with other apps and even excel spreadsheets. 
I got this because of all the overselling of the features especially the prediction feature. But I’m mostly just tolerating this app. My biggest gripe is that their big selling point the Plan feature (where you can get an estimate of what will be leftover or how much income/expenses are predicted) only works if your income and bills transactions are precisely the same each month. So if your paychecks are different amounts well then you can’t trust the numbers. Same with your expenses, if your utility bill is going to be up $100 this month well PocketGuard doesn’t know that so good luck making any smart predictions. I used to have an app that went away called Prism and that app actually connected to all your bills so it actually knew exactly what amount they would be. I miss those days. Seems like a small ask: Just tell me the exact amount of my upcoming bills please.

Also whatever tool they use the pull in the transactions could use improvement with naming conventions and how it categorizes stuff, I know that’s case by case basis but nobody gets a budgeting projection app wanting to edit every single transaction.

I highly recommend this app.

Some tips for people, here are my categories.

Instead of just Auto and Transport, I added one for GAS. Instead of just Groceries, I added SNACKS, MEAT, GUM, COOKING, KITCHEN. That way spices and oil goes into Cooking, Ziplocs and Appliances goes into Kitchen, Pickles, Mayo, Mustard goes into Groceries, Ribs, Shrimp, Eggs, Tuna, Meatballs goes into Meat (I’m doing Keto/Carnivore, and Carbs like Cookies, Chips, Ice Cream goes into Snacks. That way I can really know how much I’m spending on junk food. BOWLING, VIDEOGAMES, MOVIES, EQUIPMENT, TOOLS, BATHROOM, CASH SAVINGS, ACCESSORIES, RECURRING BILLS, SUBSCRIPTIONS, SUPPLEMENTS, GIFTS, (CASH AND ATM, TRANSFER - so I can easily see how much got added from the budget sections)

So doing this basically makes the default Pocketguard app 3X more detailed. It’s a joy to see. I’m going to spend the next 3 months dialing it in and change budgets amounts accordingly. Anything I don’t spend, like clothes, in 3 months I’d have $30 bucks saved, I could add that to my Cash Savings… If my Cash Savings gets over $1000, I could then move it to the Investments categories!

It’s always harder to spend $ when you have physical cash… you feel more guilty actually letting go of it. 

SO MY TIPS TO ANYONE!
1. Get the TurboScan app $10 lifetime
2. make a folder for _Receipts
3. everytime you buy something, scan the receipt and name it ‘YYYY.MM.DD - STORE - $$.$$’
4. Add more detailed categories
5. make a bunch of rules for stores to auto tag and categorize to help future transactions
6. 3 days later, find your Pocketguard transactions, reference your receipts, split the transactions like I explained, categorize and hashtag it, add receipt photo
7. Watch your budgets start to fill up precisely broken down to the itemized receipt
8. Have confidence knowing after a few months, you’ll know exactly what to budget for and how to plan ahead
9. Keep adding to your manually made CASH SAVINGS budget, so you always have an emergency fund
10. After 6 months, start investing everything extra that you didn’t spend!!!

TLDR - There are way better options, like Monarch.. When Mint went EOL, I, like many others, migrated to PocketGuard. I find budgeting very difficult and Mint worked extremely well for me. I read that PocketGuard was the most similar, and they have released updates that made it more similar. 

UNFORTUNATELY, PocketGuard has several fundamental flaws that make it so irritating to use that I stopped using it entirely and my finances suffered as a result. I’ll start with the good.

The good: you can set budgets and roll them over into the next month. This rollover feature was not an offering when I started using it, somehow. You can also now set rules to categorize transactions automatically which was not the case when I started using it; I initially had to recategorize every individual transaction if PocketGuard thought it belonged in a different budget. (This is still the case if the payment issuer name changes but I can’t really fault them for that.)

The bad: one of pocketguard’s selling points is its bill tracking feature. Unfortunately, this feature is actually a drawback, as whenever PocketGuard says something is a bill, it breaks it out from your budget entirely and does not let you set a monthly budget for it. This is fine for rent, but it is utterly broken for things like quarterly water bills, when the app says “scheduled for [month]” and does not count a portion of that quarterly or yearly bill towards your monthly budget. Instead, when you hit that month, suddenly you’re completely over budget because your entire quarterly water bill or annual Strava subscription or property tax is counted towards that month alone. Many times I tried to figure out a way to make this feature work for me, but it just does not. It is also a pain for the purpose of tracking things like streaming subscriptions, because even if you set an entertainment budget and categorize Spotify as entertainment, the app then DOUBLE COUNTS that recurring payment as a) a bill and b) part of your set entertainment budget. It also does not automatically deduct recurring payments such as these from your budget so that you can easily see the actual amount you have free to spend. Most of these issues have been immediately fixed for me by moving to Monarch instead. I only wish I had done so before my annual PocketGuard subscription had pinged.
